title: Get failed exports back to the coordinator

blocks.text: The nightly customer export runs on a fleet of worker JVMs. When an export fails, the job framework serializes the failure with Java serialization and sends it to the coordinator, which logs it and schedules a retry for that customer. Since the last release, the coordinator logs `java.io.NotSerializableException` where the failures used to be, and no failed export has been retried.

Workers and coordinators are upgraded on different days, so for a while a worker on one release talks to a coordinator on the other. The coordinators still run the previous release of `ExportFailedException`, which was declared with `serialVersionUID = 1L` and kept the customer's id in a `String` field named `customerId`. `Customer` comes from the CRM client library and you can't change it.

Finish `ExportFailedException` in `src/main/java/practice/Exports.java`: its constructor and `getCustomerId()`, and whatever its fields need. When you're done, a failure written on either release reaches the coordinator with its message, its cause and the id of the customer to retry. About six lines in total.

cases.says: a failure survives serialization with its message and its cause
on the worker, the failure names the customer whose export failed
after serialization the failure still names the customer, so the context is kept as serializable data rather than dropped
a failure serialized by the previous release of the class can be read by this one, because both declare the same serialVersionUID

origin.section: Every Exception Is Serializable, So Its Fields Must Be Too

concepts: Every exception is Serializable, so a non-serializable field makes serializing it fail, and transient loses the data.
An exception sent between releases declares its own serialVersionUID, or a change in the class's shape makes it unreadable.
